newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nobel laureate Tutu says cancer has spread.
newsitem.headline: Nobel laureate Tutu says cancer has spread.

text.p: South African Nobel peace laureate Desmond Tutu said on Wednesday his prostate cancer appeared to have spread and he would be treated with a combination of radiation and hormone therapy.
Tutu, 65, a leading campaigner in the fight against apartheid, said in a statement that he would go to the United States for two months later this year for the radiation therapy.
"I have been advised that the cancer is suspected to have penetrated beyond the prostate gland and that as a result radiotherapy is the best option," he said in statement.

"Medical specialists in Cape Town will begin a three-month course of hormone treatment tomorrow (Thursday)... After the hormone treatment, I plan to have the radiotherapy at a clinic in the United States," Tutu said.
Tutu, diagnosed in January as having prostate cancer, saw doctors in the United States during a visit last week.

"After discussions with medical specialists in the United States, followed by further consultations with my doctors in Cape Town, I have decided to undergo a combination of hormone treatment and radiotherapy," he said.
